𝐌𝐘 𝐂𝐈𝐍𝐄𝐌𝐀𝐓𝐈𝐂 𝐓𝐑𝐀𝐔𝐌𝐀: 𝐋𝐀 𝐋𝐀 𝐋𝐀𝐍𝐃 ❤️‍🩹⁣⁣
⁣⁣
I’ll be honest: I had no interest in seeing La La Land in 2016. I expected some lame musical where people randomly burst into song and dance. But director Damien Chazelle made a masterpiece and one that explores something much deeper: the possibility that two people can be perfect for each other, I mean PERFECT, and still not end up together.And I think that’s what makes this film so painful. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Most of us have loved someone we thought we’d spend the rest of our lives with. Someone who knew us better than anyone else. Someone we imagined growing old with, having children with, building an entire life around. And yet, for whatever reason, that person is no longer part of our lives. But don’t we all occasionally wonder what could have been? Would we still be happy together? Would we have achieved our dreams? Would we have children? What would they look like? How different would our lives be?⁣⁣
⁣⁣
Chazelle shows us exactly what we’ve all imagined at some point: an alternative life where things worked out differently. For a few minutes, we get to experience everything Sebastian and Mia could have had together. And then reality returns. One final smile, and they go their separate ways. It’s devastating. But that’s exactly what La La Land wanted us to see and feel. Sometimes the people we love help us become who we’re meant to be, even if they don’t stay in our lives. La La Land captures both the magic of falling in love and the pain of letting go, reminding us that some connections aren’t meant to last forever, but only long enough to change us. Just like in real life, things don’t always work out the way we hoped, and sometimes we’re left to walk our own paths, carrying a piece of someone we once loved along the way. ⁣⁣
⁣⁣
The last time a movie made me feel like this in a cinema, I was six years old watching Titanic (1997). I never thought I’d ever feel it again. But La La Land (2016) did it.

source_details.title: La La Land
source_details.synopsis: La La Land is a 2016 American musical romantic comedy drama film written and directed by Damien Chazelle. It stars Ryan Gosling and Emma Stone as a struggling jazz pianist and an aspiring actress who meet and fall in love while pursuing their dreams in Los Angeles. The supporting cast includes John Legend, Rosemarie DeWitt, Finn Wittrock, and J. K. Simmons. Having been fond of musicals during his time as a drummer, Chazelle first conceptualized the film alongside Justin Hurwitz while attending Harvard University together.
